themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints exploded to 4 this week versus a 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—alongside a 550% surge in curb condition complaints (13 this week vs. 2.0 avg), signaling accelerating pavement and subsurface failures across Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Curb condition complaints: 13 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (550% increase, z-score: 8.98)
Street condition ranked #5 overall complaint type in 90-day period (483 total complaints)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events (snow/ice) have exposed underlying infrastructure decay; track if ConEd or DEP has active subsurface work
Doorstep residents on residential streets showing sidewalk buckling or tree-root damage; map complaint clusters to identify worst-hit blocks

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 3 this week compared to a 0.4 weekly baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting either a new vendor concentration, health code violations, or neighborhood pushback against unregulated street commerce.
evidence: Mobile food vendor complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Spike is brand-new—appeared only in THIS WEEK data
reporting_angles: Identify which streets/intersections are drawing vendor clusters and whether they are permitted or illegal; contact Department of Health & Mental Hygiene
Interview nearby business owners and residents about quality of life impact; determine if gentrification or foot traffic changes are driving vendor activity

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints reached 12 this week versus a 3.1 weekly average—a 284% increase (z-score: 5.25)—reflecting either a surge in street-level poverty, new encampments, or heightened resident sensitivity in this affluent district.
evidence: Panhandling complaints: 12 this week vs. 3.1 weekly average (284% increase, z-score: 5.25)
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite 'other programs to address public health issues'—homelessness/poverty likely a persistent concern
Spike is concurrent with mobile food vendor surge, suggesting broader street-level economic pressure
reporting_angles: Document specific locations (subway stations, parks, commercial strips) where complaints cluster; interview unhoused individuals about recent displacement
Track if NYPD enforcement or DHS encampment clearances have driven migration into Greenwich Village/SoHo; check with local nonprofits

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 74 last week versus a 36.9 weekly average—a 101% spike (z-score: 5.28)—continuing a pattern of elevated complaints over the past 2 weeks and suggesting either weekend construction, event activity, or tenant churn.
evidence: Residential noise complaints: 74 last week vs. 36.9 weekly average (101% increase, z-score: 5.28)
Noise complaints dominate 90-day volume: residential (509), commercial (596), street/sidewalk (418)—total 1402 complaints across noise categories
1612 building alteration permits filed in last 90 days (1420 alterations alone) suggest ongoing construction activity
reporting_angles: Cross-reference noise complaint locations with active building permits to isolate construction-driven complaints; track complaint times (daytime vs. evening)
Survey residents about specific noise sources—air conditioning, late-night bars, events; connect with CB about enforcement gaps

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Exposure Risk
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 3 last week versus a 0.2 weekly baseline—a 1100% increase (z-score: 6.35)—likely tied to renovation work given the 1612 building permits filed in 90 days, posing potential public health exposure in a dense residential area.
evidence: Asbestos complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
1612 building alteration filings in last 90 days, with 1420 alterations—many older buildings likely contain asbestos materials
No corresponding increase in DOB violations or remediation orders noted in available data
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings triggered asbestos complaints; verify whether contractors filed proper DOB asbestos abatement notices; interview affected residents about exposure timeline
Investigate whether asbestos removal is being properly supervised by licensed inspectors; check for complaints to Department of Environmental Protection
